newsitem.title: UK: Investors snap up rare Cyprus Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Investors snap up rare Cyprus Eurobond.

text.p: Cyprus issued its first-ever international bond on Thursday and the deal was quickly bought by yield-hungry investors.
The $300 million five-year bond was priced to yield 37 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, a high return for a single-A rated credit.
"It was a successful issue and we were already well-oversubscribed before the bond was launched," an official at lead manager SBC Warburg said.
"The deal was popular with Swiss retail and British institutions," he added.

Cyprus, divided since Turkey invaded it in 1974, held a series of investor presentations this week to divert attention away from its political problems and towards its economic strengths. Takis Kanaris, head of economic research at the Cyprus central bank, told investors in London the country enjoyed a growth rate well above the European Union average and a high per capita gross domestic product.
GDP at current prices is projected at 4,365 million Cyprus pounds in 1997, up from a provisional 4,101 million for 1996.
Added to this, he said Cyprus had an extremely low unemployment rate -- 3.1 percent in 1996.
"In short, Cyprus enjoys economic stability, steady growth, a stable currency and clear policy objectives," Kanaris said.
The inflation rate was also consistently below the average of European countries, he said. The projected inflation rate this year is 3.2 percent, compared with 3.0 percent in 1996.
Cyprus is rated A2 by Moody's Investors Service and AA- by Standard & Poor's. The bond was issued under a $500 million Euro medium-term note (EMTN) programme recently established by Cyprus.
The proceeds will be used to refinance existing debt and to fund development projects.
On Wednesday Ioannis Ioannou, head of the external debt section at the Central Bank of Cyprus, told a conference here that it was unlikely Cyprus would launch any further bonds this year.
